title: College football winners, losers: Georgia, Wake Forest on cruise control; Kentucky craters - CBS Sports
description: Georgia asserts its championship pedigree and Wake Forest sends a message, while Kentucky's playoff dreams evapor
body:
Georgia asserts its championship pedigree and Wake Forest sends a message, while Kentucky's playoff dreams evaporate and USC continues to unravel
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College football's Week 11 didn't feature quite as many fireworks as previous weeks. Instead, it turned into a prove-it Saturday for the College Football Playoff contenders. No. 1 Georgia cemented itself as the best team in the nation with an obliteration of Missouri, while No. 13 Wake Forest proved they belonged in the mix. No. 11 Kentucky lost a heartbreaker to Florida to likely end their chances, while No. 14 Houston pushed itself into purgatory. In the night slate, No. 2 Utah will try to end a streak of five straight. No. 6 Texas also tries to hold off No. 21 LSU and cement a slot in the College Football Playoff. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 11. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: GeorgiaThe Dawgs are back in business after a sensational performance against No. 22 Missouri. The Bulldogs ground the Tigers into a fine powder, taking a 31-0 lead barely halfway through the second quarter. The 48-21 win -- led by three touchdowns from running back Nate Frazier -- only continued a stretch of impressive play from Georgia. 
Over a period of just under 10 quarters, Georgia outscored opponents 100-15. All three of those games were against teams ranked at the time, headlined by a 42-7 win over No. 10 Ole Miss. Georgia looks like championship Georgia again. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: KentuckyKentucky coach Will Stein launched himself to the top of national coach of the year boards midseason after leading the Wildcats to an incredible 7-1 start and a No. 6 CFP Ranking. Unfortunately, despite a worthy effort, the season is quickly crashing to the ground. The Wildcats lost a heartbreaker, 21-14, to a struggling Florida team. Kentucky allowed a 14-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter and threw four straight incompletions with a chance to go and win the game. Now, Kentucky's playoff hopes are virtually dead, opening the door for numerous other contenders to get in the mix. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Wake ForestThe Demon Deacons haven't gotten much respect during their run to 9-1, and poor SMU was the target of their wrath. Wake Forest absolutely obliterated the Mustangs 49-7, taking a 42-0 lead in the first half.Wake Forest has dominated teams in every phase of the game, both outpassing and outrushing opponents over the past six games. Quarterback Gio Lopez has been especially good, throwing for 19 touchdowns to only one interception. The Demon Deacons don't beat themselves, and those successes add up. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: USCThe Trojans' win over Ohio State sure looks like a major indictment of the Buckeyes because outside of that game, USC has been horrible. USC lost 27-13 against No. 9 Indiana as the Hoosiers made a quarterback change. In his first start as the guy, Grant Wilson threw for 305 yards and two touchdowns against a lackluster USC defense. 
Outside of Ohio State, USC lost by a combined 28 points against their two ranked opponents. Their other Big Ten wins are by a combined 19 points. The Trojans are wildly underperforming, and Indiana helped show their cracks. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: RB Aidan Flora, Iowa StateIt's time to have a conversation about Aidan Flora. The Iowa State running back was an afterthought in the program under Matt Campbell. Instead, he just might be the best running back in America. Flora exploded for 216 yards and three touchdowns, his third straight game of at least 180 yards and a touchdown. With the performance, Flora is now up to 1,335 yards, which could lead the nation depending on how the night ends. Iowa State is now in position to make a bowl game with one win in the final two, and Flora is the primary reason why. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: WisconsinAll of the good vibes around Luke Fickell are officially gone after the Badgers lost an embarrassing matchup, 24-21, against interim-coached Maryland. The Terrapins were without starting quarterback Malik Washington and had not beaten consecutive Big Ten teams since 2023, but the Badgers completely collapsed. Wisconsin allowed 10 unanswered points in the last 2:11 to blow a fourth-quarter lead, marking their second loss in three games. The Badgers will be favored against Purdue and Minnesota to end the year, but would a 7-5 campaign really be good enough, given all the investment in the program? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Georgia Tech coach Brent KeyGeorgia Tech's season is a lost cause, but the Yellow Jackets found a little bit of hope. The team outplayed Clemson in a 20-6 victory, the first win over the Tigers since Dabo Swinney's first season in 2008. 
Jackets coach Brent Key made a few aggressive moves earlier this week, firing defensive coordinator Jason Semore and three other assistants. The unit played its best game of the season, holding Clemson to only six points and 86 yards rushing, with Vinnie Sunseri calling the plays.

body:
Since an upset loss to Auburn, Georgia, has left a series of lopsided scores and decimated foes in its wake and looks like the best team in the country by a fair margin
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the wake of its loss to Auburn, Georgia faced serious questions. In the three weeks since their open date, the Bulldogs have not only answered those questions, but they've been head and shoulders above any other team in college football.Saturday's 48-21 win over Missouri was the latest in a series of Bulldog demolitions. In its last three games -- all against ranked opponents -- Georgia is 3-0 with a plus-81 point differential. The 2026 Bulldogs are just the eighth team in AP poll history to beat three consecutive ranked opponents by at least 17 points.The last team to do that was the 2021 Georgia squad, and that team went on to win the national championship. At this point, it's easy to imagine this year's team doing the exact same thing.Since that open date, Georgia has been firing on all cylinders in every aspect of the game. The defense is playing like a vintage Kirby Smart unit, and the offense is scoring at will.
For most of the season, the national championship race seemed pretty wide open. Lately, it's looked a lot more like Georgia versus the field. At the moment, the field doesn't look all that appealing.Dominating defenseGeorgia has fielded some elite defenses under Smart, and this particular unit may not stack up to the best of those, but its working its way up the list.Over the last three games combined, the Bulldogs have allowed seven points in the first half. Once teams start to move the ball against Georgia, if they do at all, it's after the game is already in hand. Even with garbage-time yardage factored in, the numbers have been pretty staggering.
Georgia defense: Last three games12.0 points against per game263.3 yards allowed per game9 sacks17 tackles for loss7 turnovers forcedIt's not like the Bulldogs have done this against a bunch of tomato cans either. Admittedly, the Florida offense is a mess, but that can't be said for Ole Miss or Missouri. Entering the day, the Rebels and Tigers were top-five SEC offenses in total yards, and they were both averaging more than 30 points per game.This defense is playing well enough to win games on its own, but it doesn't have to do that because the offense has been excellent.Offense is hummingIn the wake of Georgia's 27-8 win over Florida, I wrote about the questions still facing Gunner Stockton and the passing attack. I've had some stories age poorly, but this is easily the fastest I've been made to look the fool.
Over the last two games, Stockton has silenced doubters like myself with wildly efficient performances. His raw yardage totals won't jump off the page, but his 11.2 yards per attempt will. He's also completed 69.2 percent of his passes with five touchdowns and zero interceptions.Just for good measure, Stockton has flexed his mobility with 34 rushing yards and a pair of touchdowns on the ground.Speaking of the ground game, that's been the engine driving these Bulldogs lately. Using a rotation in the backfield, Georgia has been grinding teams into a pulp with its rushing attack. Since the open date, the Dawgs are averaging 231.1 rushing yards per game. This win over Missouri was their lowest total at 181 yards.
Coming into the day, Georgia led the SEC with 41.1 points per game. That number will only climb after its thrashing off Missouri, and in a season with few truly elite offenses, the Bulldogs have one of the best in the country.Can anyone slow down the Dawgs?Georgia has simply been on another level the last few weeks. How many other teams can realistically match the Bulldogs?Notre Dame has a win over Miami on its resume, but that Hurricanes defense can be exploited through the air. With Ellis Robinson IV and KJ Bolden in the defensive backfield, that's not the case with Georgia.
If the Hurricanes get Malachi Toney back for the College Football Playoff, they are one of the few teams that could really stress the Bulldogs defense. The question there is whether Toney will be himself coming off ankle surgery next month.What about Alabama? Georgia has already gone on the road and beaten the Crimson Tide in Tuscaloosa, albeit by a slim margin. Besides, this Georgia offense looks much stronger now than it did then.Teams like Indiana and Texas have elite defenses but too many questions on offense. If the Longhorns' weapons all played up to their potential, they're capable of beating the Bulldogs, but how many times has that happend this season? Not often enough.
It's just hard to see anyone beating Georgia if it plays its best game. The Bulldogs are too good on both sides of the ball when they're at their best.They weren't against Auburn, but that loss may have been a blessing in disguise. Ever since that game, Georgia has been unaffected by the newfound parity of college football, bludgeoning every team it meets onthe road to another national championship.

        WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames took a trip up to the super middleweight division in the main event of Saturday's Zuffa Boxing 13. Adames picked up a win over Gerome Warburton, earning a clear decision victory over an opponent who rarely seemed interested in providing any offensive resistance.The fight was anything but exciting in the opening rounds, with both Adames and Warburton doing more staring and posturing than punching. If the idea was that Adames would immediately bring the fight to Warburton, making the more unknown commodity feel as though he was entering a level he was not ready for, Adames seemed hesitant to put that idea into action.Adames started to turn up the pressure slightly by the third round, and even more around the fifth. Warburton was content to circle around the perimeter of the ring, largely at the insistance of his corner than he "continue boxing," but that allowed Adames, even in slow rounds, to appear to be in control by simply being willing to engage.Sign up for Paramount+ and watch Zuffa Boxing for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Adames kept a strong focus on Warburton's body, likely knowing the only time Warburton had been stopped was due to a relentless body attack by Kieron Conway. A big hook to the body from Adames in the seventh round seemed to freeze Warburton, an effect of the body work adding up round after round.In the moments where Warburton felt confident enough to throw punches, he had brief moments of success, but those times were rare as he spent more time moving and reacting than sitting down and letting his hands go.Warburton's confidence issues were on display between rounds, as he asked his corner if he'd won even a single round. By the end of the ninth round, Warburton was spending the final stretch of the round actively disengaging from the fight before talking to Adames after the bell. The juxtaposition of action between the bells was odd for Warburton, who was being given the biggest opportunity of his career, even if a world title wasn't on the line.
Warburton managed to survive the final round, achieving something of a moral victory that he'd gone the distance with the best middleweight in the game, even going as far as to celebrate on the ropes and dance after the final bell despite likely having lost every round. If it was a moral victory for Warburton, it was a moral victory the larger boxing world will likely not respect or remember.At the end of 10 rounds, the final scorecards read 100-90, 99-91, 98-92, all for Adames."I think he was just in the ring to survive, he wasn't really here to win the fight," Adames said after the fight. "He could have done more, but he wasn't really a match. I think he could of done more but I think he was just surviving."
For Adames, Saturday will not go down as one of his most memorable trips to the ring, but a win is a win and Adames avoided a significant stumble, even outside of his middleweight home. Now, he can turn his attention back to establishing himself as the best middleweight in the world."I could say I could fight whoever I want," Adames said. "But the real question is who wants to fight Carlos Adames?"

Whittingham was a late arrival in the coaching carousel and could be one-and-done in Ann Arbor

        The Kyle Whittingham era in Ann Arbor got off to an inauspicious start as the Michigan Wolverines needed a miraculous (and controversial) Hail Mary just to beat Western Michigan in their opener. Things briefly stabilized with a win over Oklahoma, but the Wolverines hit a new low when they lost 15-6 at home to rival Michigan State in Week 10. After firing their highly paid offensive coordinator Jason Beck following the loss to Michigan State, Whittingham desperately needed his Wolverines to show improvement on the road at Oregon in Week 11. That did not happen as Michigan once again failed to reach double digits on the scoreboard in a 31-7 loss in which they benched Tommy Carr to go back to Bryce Underwood to no avail. Whittingham arrived at Michigan late in the coaching carousel after Sherrone Moore was fired after an investigation into an inappropriate relationship with a staffer. The longtime coach at Utah stepped down in Salt Lake City after 20 years as the Utes' coach -- and more than 30 years on the Utah staff -- and arrived at Michigan tasked with resetting the culture in Ann Arbor. As an outsider to the Michigan program, Whittingham needed to win over some in the fan base by proving he still has what it takes to make a team a contender, but his first season in charge has done little to quell concerns that he's past his prime as a program builder. 
Michigan fans are already antsy about the program falling from its perch in the Big Ten's top tier, and even though it's Whittingham's first year in charge, the expectation was that the veteran coach would bring stability and discipline. Instead, the Wolverines have been sloppy and ineffective on offense -- no matter which quarterback is under center -- and while the defense remains stout, it cannot make up for their offensive ineptitude. That has raised the temperature under Whittingham considerably, and some Wolverines fans have already seen enough. Unlike some other programs that have to strongly weigh the financial pros and cons of moving on from an embattled coach, Whittingham's contract seemed designed to allow Michigan to pull the plug whenever they felt they needed to. Not all losses are created equal, and after handing their in-state rivals their first Big Ten win of Pat Fitzgerald's first season in charge, chatter about Whittingham's job picked up considerably. Another lopsided loss at Oregon did nothing to quiet the noise, and Michigan boosters may be passing the hat soon. 
Kyle Whittingham buyout, contract detailsWhittingham signed a five-year, $41 million contract this offseason to take over the Wolverines, which is a relative bargain for a program with deep pockets like Michigan. His buyout percentage is also quite low at 75% (one of the lowest in the Big Ten), which means the Wolverines could move on from Whittingham after just one season in charge for the price of $24.75 million.Given that a new athletic director will take over at Michigan in 2027 after Warde Manuel steps down, Whittingham will not have much institutional backing and will need to see the Wolverines improve considerably if he's going to make it to a second year in charge. His hire already felt like a stopgap after the sudden dismissal of Moore, but the hope was he could rebuild a culture of winning to set Michigan's next coach up for immediate success. Instead, Michigan now has to consider whether it's worth continuing Whittingham's tenure and trying to find a new quarterback in the portal, or whether it wants to bite the bullet on around $25 million to become the best job on the market this offseason (at least so far).

title: Washington Spirit clinch third consecutive trip to NWSL Championship with win over Utah Royals - CBS Sports
description: The Spirit will host the championship game at Audi Field on Saturday Nov. 21
body:
The Spirit will host the championship game at Audi Field on Saturday Nov. 21
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After two runner-up finishes at the NWSL Championship, the Washington Spirit will get a third consecutive shot at lifting the big prize.The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field. The Spirit weathered the fastest goal in NWSL playoff history, then flipped the script within minutes and never took their foot off the pedal or lost control. Utah Royals' Cloe Lacasse struck first on the scoreboard, and Sofia Cantore and Clara Luvanga provided the decisive goals for the Spirit, while Trinity Rodman brought plenty of spark and Andi Sullivan supplied reliable, steady play in the midfield.Here's how the Spirit rallied for the win:Utah's set-piece historyThe Royals arrived in D.C. early in the week, avoiding a nationwide flight stoppage on Friday, and fresh off a huge quarterfinal upset -- a 1-0 win against the No. 2 seed San Diego Wave FC. They wasted little time to show their early playoff win was no fluke.In the opening two minutes, Utah won a corner kick, and Lacasse created multiple moments of history. Her service into the box curled toward the near post, creating some miscommunication between goalkeeper Sandy MacIver and her defenders, and the ball snuck into the net. It was the fastest goal scored in NWSL playoff history and the first-ever olimpico scored in the postseason. 
The early breakthrough stunned the typically rowdy crowd, though the set-piece tally was hardly a surprise, considering Utah's ability this year. The squad scored 15 goals off set pieces this season, with seven headed goals, so Lacasse's ability to score from the flag was just one more highlight for its set-piece playbook.The early lead should have been a boost for the visiting side, but instead, it opened up the game; the Spirit then tested the Royals with relentless attacking pressure.Washington Spirit's rapid responseThe Spirit needed just six minutes to turn things around. Washington's attacking trio combined for the equalizer, with Luvanga finding Rodman out wide in space, and the winger quickly connecting with Cantore in front of goal. 
"I think getting scored on in the first few minutes will really humble you, and a little bit of a wake-up call, but I thought our response was incredible right after and all game long," Sullivan said after the game."As soon as we responded after the goal, I think even when we got scored on, I had full confidence that we would get it done," she said.Sullivan's role in controlling the game as the Spirit closed out the first half was notable. She's the longest-tenured player on the active Spirit roster right now, with goalkeeper Aubrey Kingsbury out on maternity leave. Sullivan herself returned to the squad after an ACL injury and then maternity leave. The defensive midfielder completed all of her tackles (three) and aerial challenges (four) and captained the team on the pitch.
"She represents a lot of the values that we want to have as a team, as a club, on and off the field, and right now she's reaching that peak of performance. I'm very, very happy and proud of her because it's been tough for her. Obviously, coming from a long injury, and then maternity leave. So being able to come back to get fit again and try to compete at this level; it's not easy, and she's a role model. An example as a captain with the young players, new players, and being able to do a lot of things," Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez said after the game."Whatever the team needs, she's kind of that voice. Very happy and proud of her because I know what this means to her and also for us. Having her again and being able to play a final is huge for her and for us," he said.Controlling the second halfWhile Utah managed to stave off attacking sequences by the Spirit to close out the opening half, the Spirit's game-winning goal came in the early minutes of the second half. A poor back pass by Utah in their own half was the final dagger. Luvanga pounced on the mistimed pass, and a smart touch inside the box beat goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn. 
The Tanzanian international has only been on the roster since September, but her impact on games has grown week to week, and now she can add a game-winning NWSL playoff goal to her resume."It's not the first one that she scores like that. Obviously, she puts a lot of pressure on centerbacks, keepers, and that is very contagious. When you see that your forward is pushing and jumping and pressing like that. Everyone who is behind they follow her, and also creates a lot of doubts and nerves on the opponent team, not facilitating the build-up. And obviously, that was, I think, a big shot of energy," Gonzalez said after the game."I think it was also a little bit of release, knowing that 'okay, we did the most difficult thing' that was coming back after we conceded a goal, and yeah, happy again because she's bringing a lot. Both attacking and defending, and obviously she's learning so quick and having a huge impact."
What's next The Spirit will face the winner of Sunday's semifinal between Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current. This will be the Spirit's third consecutive appearance in the NWSL Championship. When the league announced a neutral site for the 2026 NWSL Championship, it selected Audi Field, and now the Spirit have a chance to play in a home playoff final on Nov. 21.

A 42-point road rout over SMU kept the Demon Deacons on the brink of the College Football Playoff while pushing their first-half scoring margin to 145-0 over the last four games

        DALLAS -- There's no good reason Wake Forest should be doing this. Quarterback Gio Lopez was thrown to the dustpile after a miserable season at North Carolina last season. Their coach, Jake Dickert, only became a head coach after his boss was fired at Washington State. They're No. 65 in the 247Sports Talent Composite. The Demon Deacons lost high-profile transfers to Texas, Florida and Texas Tech, simply unable to keep up with the financial demands. Their replacements came from FIU, New Hampshire and Weber State. It doesn't matter.No. 13 Wake Forest went on the road and obliterated SMU 49-7, one of the most dominant performances of the season by any team. They've outscored their opponents 145-0 over the last four games -- in the first half. The Demon Deacons have arrived. And they're spectacular. "I think people don't know what to make of us because they don't understand how we're doing it," Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert said. "I think we keep making statement after statement, eventually they're going to have to say we're a pretty good team." 
Winning in every phaseWake Forest has been dominant since losing to Miami, but this one came with something a little extra. The Mustangs were narrow 1.5-point favorites coming in, and had a big opportunity to play their way back into ACC contention with a win. After going down 7-0, SMU coach Rhett Lashlee went for it on an early fourth down. Wake Forest stuffed them at the line, and swung the game with a touchdown five plays later. They scored again on the third and fourth drives, the latter off a swing pass fumble, to push the lead out to 28-0 in an instant. Wake Forest outgained SMU (535-275), outpassed them (249-209), outrushed them (286-66), held the ball longer (37:00-23:00) and turnovers (3-1). SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings, who ranks among the most productive players in college football, was held to only 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception. What was built to be a celebration of Jennings' last game at Gerald J. Ford Stadium turned into a nightmare. 
"They whipped us in every area you can whip someone in a football game," Lashlee told reporters. But for Wake Forest, this has been a trend. They rank No. 3 in the ACC in offense and No. 2 in defense. They dragged down Jennings and the passing offense against SMU, but also limited Miami's elite rushing offense to 158 yards, one of their most middling performances of the season. They've outgained, outscored, outpassed and outrushed each of their last six opponents. The Demon Deacons can beat you any way on any day. They're just that good.
"The defense is firing on all cylinders," linebacker Aiden Hall said. "It's not much that I can say bad about what we're doing right now… we can't control who recognizes us or who doesn't. Only thing we can control is how bad we keep whooping on teams."Prime positionAfter the win, Wake Forest is right on the cusp of crashing the College Football Playoff. The Demon Deacons sit at No. 13, and could rise following a dominant performance against a top 40 opponent. The quarterback Lopez and wide receiver Carlos Hernandez will get serious All-America consideration with their strong performance. Otherwise, the rest of the team takes pride in being "Built in the Dark," Dickert's motto. 
If Wake Forest can beat Georgia Tech and Duke over the next two weeks, they'll set up a rematch against Miami in the ACC title game. Especially with wide receiver Malachi Toney still sidelined, the Demon Deacons could win their first ACC title since 2006 and crash the postseason. Everything is on the table in Winston-Salem, only emphasized after Dickert and heralded offensive coordinator Rob Ezell signed extensions to stay with the program. "The biggest thing is, I don't want people to think what we're doing right now is easy," Dickert said. "We're one of the lowest payroll teams in the country and people assume certain things about our guys, our coaches, our university, and it's not true. That's part of why I stayed here, right? There's a pathway to creating success at a place like Wake…
"You want to be coached in football and you want to develop? Come to Wake Forest."

title: Championship hangover? Josh Hart 'not in a good headspace' as he, other Knicks struggle amid uneven start - CBS Sports
description: The vibes have shifted for the Knicks early in their title defense
body:
The vibes have shifted for the Knicks early in their title defense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 14, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The New York Knicks slipped to 6-6 on Friday with a 106-104 loss to the Indiana Pacers, dropping into a tie for fifth in the Eastern Conference alongside the Miami Heat. While it hasn't been an outright disaster of a start, it has been an uneven performance by the defending champions that has left them frustrated and searching for answers. The championship hangover in New York seems to be real, and the once immaculate vibes at Madison Square Garden have been replaced by frustration as they try to get on track. After a scoreless performance against the Pacers, Josh Hart was brutally honest about not knowing what's wrong and how he's been struggling mentally to start this season. "Wish I could tell you," Hart said. "Don't know. Right now I'm not in a good headspace, and I got to figure out how to improve that and improve my play."
New York's wing woesOne of the strengths of the Knicks during their title run last year was their rotation of two-way wings between Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, but so far this season their three best wings -- OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Hart -- have been stuck in the mud offensively. Those three are all shooting below 40% from the field and below 33% from 3-point range this season, a massive departure from last season when they were all above 48% from the field and 37% from distance. The result of New York's wings struggling on offense -- aside from Landry Shamet, who has been a needed bright spot -- has been an even greater burden on Brunson and Towns. Towns has been sensational, averaging 21.1 points and 13.7 rebounds per game on 54.2/40.0/77.0 shooting splits as he's moved back to a full-time role at center after the departure of Mitchell Robinson. Brunson has been his typically excellent self, averaging 26.6 points and 5.7 assists per game -- a slim uptick in points and a small decrease in assists from last year -- but his efficiency has dipped, shooting 43.6% from the field. 
While his 3-point percentage has held firm at 37.5%, he's shooting just 55.8% from inside three feet. That would be the worst finishing rate of his career at the rim and seems to be a byproduct of teams collapsing in without the threat of spacing from the wings around Brunson. A less effective Brunson at the rim, the struggles of their wings and Towns playing more at the five have resulted in a Knicks offense that is 29th in the NBA in paint points at 35.5%. Mike Brown's offense is predicated on launching threes, but a year ago the Knicks got 41.4% of their points in the paint. A 6% drop-off there is a significant reduction, especially considering how poorly they're shooting from three as a team. The post-championship vibe shiftThe big question raised by Hart's comments after Indiana's game is: how did the Knicks get here after winning the title? 
It's one thing to have a championship hangover, but it's another to have the vibes of a team sour so quickly, considering their success was built in no small part on being a tight-knit group. It's hard not to point to the top of the organization and the way James Dolan seemed adamant about raining on the Knicks' championship celebration almost as soon as it began. Dolan didn't even let the champagne-soaked locker room dry out before he proclaimed his refusal to go into the second apron to keep the team together. He stayed true to his word, letting Robinson walk to the rival Boston Celtics. However, what was perhaps more impactful on this year's poor start is the way the Knicks handled extension talks with much of their roster. 
        
            
                Karl-Anthony Towns contract: What to know as Knicks enter season with question marks
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Towns made clear his desire to work out a deal to stay in New York and cut the Knicks a hometown discount, but New York was asking him to take an even bigger pay cut than he was willing. Ultimately, talks fell apart and the Knicks made the curious decision to publicly announce they were no longer going to discuss extensions with anyone on the roster a week before the season began. 
Hart is among the extension-eligible players, but unlike Towns, who can decline a player option and hit free agency, his option for next year is a $22.3 million team option. If the Knicks wanted, they could simply pick up Hart's option and extend discussions on a new deal into next summer. One can't help but wonder whether the uncertainty about the future is part of whatis affecting Hart and putting him in a bad headspace. Some players thrive under the pressure of a contract year, while others just feel the anxiety of not having a stable future. Hart, whose impact often goes beyond the box score, might feel that more than others. The Knicks had two paths they could've taken this summer after winning their first title in over 50 years. One was to do everything possible to lock up the core group as quickly as possible and try to keep the good vibes rolling. The other was to play hardball and use the championship as an opportunity to squeeze players for a discount. 
Knicks fans weren't surprised to see Dolan choose option two, and now they have to wonder if that's at the root of an uneven start to their title defense.

The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline.         The New England Patriots and Detroit Lions are headed to Germany this week. The teams will kick off Sunday's action with a 9:30 a.m. game at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins. The victory extended their win streak to four games.Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings. The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers. In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11).The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East.
Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to knowInjuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness.Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs (DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production.International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying, "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans."Lions vs. Patriots where to watchDate: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ETLocation: Allianz Arena (Munich, Germany)TV: Fox | Stream: fubo (free trial available)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Lions -2.5 (via DraftKings)
Lions vs. Patriots predictionI think the Patriots will make some adjustments from last week and come out stronger in Week 10. This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win.  Pick: Patriots 33, Lions 30

body:
Boston could move on from once-promising outfielders Kristian Campbell and Jarren Duran this winter

        LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this. With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy? For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell. Tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a big-league game in 2026, is currently on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors. 
Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy. Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question."I'm not going to speak to that right now," he said "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of." 
Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.
        
            
                How a polarizing hitting approach took over MLB, and what happened when it stopped working for a top prospect
                
                    Julian McWilliams                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract. Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club. 
None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels."He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright big-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field." 
Jake Bauers The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time. Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway. With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.
One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade. Naturally, there is some apprehension. "I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow said. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately."
Other notesRangers president of baseball operations Chris Young made it known that his team isn't trying to rebuild entering next season. The Rangers have failed to make the playoffs in the three years following their first-ever World Series title in 2023. Still veterans Corey Seager and Jacob deGrom remain on the trade block for the Rangers as they try to shed high-salary players and retool.When agent Scott Boras was asked if the Reds could keep his client, Elly De La Cruz, Boras responded, "Well, the idea of what ownership does and what they choose to do is that they have to understand how they operate and why they operate," he said. "If I'm going to operate like I did 20 years ago and everybody in my division is operating differently, I'm not going to be able to capitalize the franchise to a level that others have to create an opportunity." The Reds looked promising just a year ago, making the postseason in 2025 for the first time in five years. The Reds have made it known to other teams that they are willing to discuss their starting pitching.Starter Sonny Gray reconciled his grievance with the Red Sox after publicly criticizing his early removal from Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Gray reached out shortly after his comments that evening. The right-hander would be willing to return to Boston, but the league-wide belief is that he ends up closer to his Nashville home. The Braves, who need starting pitching, are seen as the frontrunner for his services.
